title: A search using GEO600 for gravitational waves coincident with fast radio bursts from SGR 1935+2154
venue: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
extended_summary:
This paper is not an education or ChatGPT mathematics intervention study. It reports an astrophysical search for gravitational-wave emission coincident with fast radio bursts from the magnetar SGR 1935+2154, using GEO600 data collected during four FRB activity periods. The authors also examine nearby X-ray glitches and bursts observed by NICER and NuSTAR in 2022 October.

The intervention/approach is a pair of unmodeled gravitational-wave burst searches: PySTAMP for long-duration signals (1–10 s) and X-Pipeline for short-duration signals (<1 s). The analysis uses single-detector GEO600 data because the LIGO and Virgo detectors were offline during the relevant FRBs; the paper therefore constructs on-source and off-source windows, injects simulated waveforms, and estimates upper limits on gravitational-wave energy rather than testing an educational treatment.

The source context is an isolated magnetar in the Milky Way, not a student population. The authors find no significant gravitational-wave candidates associated with any FRB or X-ray event. They report upper limits on emitted gravitational-wave energy and on the GW-to-radio energy ratio, improving on prior FRB coincidence limits at some frequencies and providing the first long-duration FRB-coincident constraints for this source. Because this paper is unrelated to education, no comparator evidence for grades 6–8 ChatGPT mathematics interventions is present.
quality_tier_rationale: This is not an education study and does not evaluate any educational technology or AI intervention. It is a peer-reviewed astrophysics paper using GW search pipelines, not a K-12 empirical intervention study.
impact_tier_rationale: There is no educational impact to extract for the requested topic. The closest comparator evidence is absent because the paper contains no ChatGPT, mathematics, grades 6–8, or counterfactual educational intervention.
